title: Unraveling dental caries misinformation: Identifying predictive factors for engagement on Instagram
screen_reason: Content analysis of 500 English-language Instagram posts about dental caries, each coded by two trained investigators as information or misinformation against scientific guidelines/consensus statements; reports the share of posts classified misinformation (220/500 = 44.0%). That is a quantitative share of items with a denominator, judged against an external ground truth, so it meets the CONTENT criterion.

estimates.country: English-language posts; authors state the evaluation was restricted to Instagram posts from English-speaking countries (no country list given)
estimates.date: Posts published between August 2018 and August 2022
estimates.measure_type: % of dental-caries Instagram posts classified as misinformation
estimates.denominator: 500 English-language Instagram posts about dental caries, drawn from the 10,000 highest-interaction posts retrieved by CrowdTangle keyword/hashtag search and screened down through the first 2,063 posts
estimates.definition: A post was counted in the numerator when two independent coders judged that it disseminated false or misleading content about dental caries, assessed against scientific guidelines, consensus statements and systematic reviews (e.g. a post contradicting the evidence for fluoridated toothpaste, or claiming antibiotics cause caries)
estimates.misinfo_def: "The term 'misinformation' was used in this study to broadly describe false or incorrect information, encompassing 'misinformation' (unintentional errors) and 'disinformation' (deliberate deception intended to harm)."
estimates.source_quote: A total of 220 posts (44.0%) classiﬁed misinformation
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 4; also Abstract ('Misinformation accounted for 44% of posts') and Table 1, Facticity row (Information 280 (56.0%) / Misinformation 220 (44.0%))
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two trained clinical dentists (TSM, AMJ) coded independently after intra-examiner calibration on 10% of posts (n = 50) with a third experienced researcher (TC); calibration ICC exceeded 0.7 for all categories and ICC values for the final calibration ranged 0.76-0.87; disagreements resolved by discussion to consensus. Truth benchmark was scientific guidelines, consensus statements and systematic reviews on dental caries (AAPD reference manual; Schwendicke et al. Delphi consensus).
estimates.moderator_quote: A search strategy was developed by the association of representative terms and hashtags using Boolean operators, as follows: "dental decay" OR "tooth decay" OR "toothdecay" OR "cavities" OR "cavities" OR "carious lesion" OR "carious-lesion" OR "caries" OR "cavity". The data collection focused on posts with the highest total interaction published between August 2018 and August 2022, filtered by photos and albums.
estimates.notes: Single-issue keyword corpus (dental caries) hence denom_scope=topical; the sample is rank-truncated to the highest-interaction posts, hence denom_selection=curated - the 44% is a share of highly-engaged posts, not of all caries posts on Instagram. Data collection spans Aug 2018-Aug 2022; year coded as the end of the collection window. Country is not reported: only that posts were English-language and the authors describe them as coming from English-speaking countries, so coded Global. Quote trimmed to the single verbatim line fragment carrying the value; the rest of the sentence (shares by user type, format, topic and sentiment) continues on interleaved print lines. The abstract states the same figure: 'Misinformation accounted for 44% of posts.'

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Table 2 breaks misinformation down by aim of content (prevention 114/239 = 47.7%; treatment 106/261 = 40.6%). These are within-paper subgroups of the same 500-post sample rather than a separate country/platform/measure, and they are not the paper's headline figure, so no sub-rows were created (per the rule against inventing sub-rows and keeping the main figure). Note also an internal inconsistency in the paper: the Table 2 column headers read 'n = 293' (prevention) and 'n = 207' (treatment) while the cell counts sum to 239 and 261, matching Table 1's aim-of-content split; the header numbers appear to be a typographical error. (2) The Discussion cites a previous study reporting 40.8% of Facebook posts on dental caries contained misinformation (ref 16) - a figure from elsewhere, so not extracted (R8). (3) Table 1 medians of total interactions and overperforming score by facticity, and the Table 3 odds ratios, are association statistics, not prevalence shares, so not extracted. (4) The other descriptive shares (67.8% regular users, 61% photo format, 73.8% positive sentiment, 52.2% treatment-focused) describe post attributes, not misinformation, so are not estimates for this review.

rob.design: Cross-sectional infodemiology content analysis. Frame: CrowdTangle keyword/hashtag search of English-language Instagram posts on dental caries published Aug 2018-Aug 2022, ranked by total interactions; 10,000 posts retrieved, the first 2,063 screened by one independent researcher (exclusions: off-topic n=128, non-English n=25, inaccessible links n=29, duplicates n=1,381) to yield a fixed target sample of 500 posts. No response rate applies (observational platform data). Coding: two trained, calibrated dentist coders independently applied a deductive framework (author profile, sentiment, motivation, format, aim, facticity), calibrated on 10% (n=50) with a third researcher; calibration ICC > 0.7 for all categories, final ICC 0.76-0.87; disagreements resolved by consensus discussion. Falsity judged against scientific guidelines, consensus statements and systematic reviews. Limitations acknowledged by the authors: English-only, no regional variation, limited sample size. Raw data deposited on Figshare.
rob.item6_quote: In this sense, posts were classified as misinformation when they disseminated false or misleading content, following scientific guidelines, consensus statements, and systematic reviews to evaluate information on dental caries.
rob.item10_quote: A total of 220 posts (44.0%) classified misinformation, with the most being shared by regular users (n = 339, 67.8%), in photo format (n = 305, 61%), focusing on the treatment of dental caries (n = 261, 52.2%), and expressing a positive sentiment (n = 369, 73.8%).
